evidence_fault: March 1 follow-up, job processing: The library could not decode otherwise valid responses, preventing Actions from queuing jobs.

evidence_trigger: January 28, cause paragraph: GitHub traced the incident to its SQL layer but did not identify what initiated the database failure.
evidence_fault: January 28, impact and cause paragraphs: The database failure disrupted an internal Actions dependency; monitors detected service errors, and queued jobs failed or were delayed.

evidence_trigger: November 27 follow-up: A rare condition generated an unusually high volume of GitHub App token requests.
evidence_fault: November 27 follow-up: Amplified queries overloaded MySQL, leaving replicas behind and causing some Actions token requests to fail.

evidence_trigger: November 2 incident: The certificate reached its expiration date before the team acted on the automated warning.
evidence_fault: November 2 incident: The expired wildcard certificate affected web requests for GitHub’s interface and services.

evidence_trigger: October 9, paragraph 1: During scheduled ZooKeeper reprovisioning, hosts were added too rapidly, leading to a second leader election.
evidence_fault: October 9, paragraphs 2–3: Conflicting Kafka cluster states caused about one in ten background job writes to fail, and queues backed up.

evidence_trigger: September 17 incident: The report does not identify what made one Pages node stop accepting builds.
evidence_fault: September 17 incident: One node remained available for site requests but failed every build routed to it until staff disabled it.

evidence_trigger: July 13 follow-up: GitHub describes deployment changes made after the incident but does not identify what started it.
evidence_fault: July 13 follow-up: Restarting containers depended on the registry, but GitHub does not say the registry was unavailable or identify a component failure.

evidence_trigger: Preliminary Root Cause: An internal infrastructure problem disrupted scale-out, but the report does not identify what started the problem.
evidence_fault: Preliminary Root Cause: High CPU utilization degraded Graph API performance and caused timeout errors.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: Faulty router memory disrupted synchronization between the control and data planes during routine maintenance.
evidence_fault: Root Cause: The router dropped packets for some destinations, disrupting new SQL connections and impairing App Service operations that depended on SQL.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: A regional workload surge triggered the backlog while maintenance was underway.
evidence_fault: Root Cause and Summary of Impact: Queued requests took longer to process; users encountered sign-in or sign-up errors and timeouts.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: The Allocator service failed in one zone before retries surged; the report does not identify what caused the Allocator failure.
evidence_fault: Root Cause: Allocator unavailability triggered retries that overwhelmed the gateway. Continued retries prolonged the impact, and many gateway calls failed with timeout exceptions.

evidence_trigger: Cause section: Azure increased database capacity to handle demand, exposing an existing bug in how the ACS resource provider processed query results.
evidence_fault: Cause and response sections: Database requests had reached the throughput limit before scaling. After scaling, authentication failed across regions, causing customer API requests to fail.

evidence_trigger: Cause section: During planned capacity expansion, the topology update mistakenly marked unconnected links as active.
evidence_fault: Cause and impact sections: Incorrect topology data prompted healthy link shutdowns, congesting remaining paths. Packet loss peaked at 10%; some resources faced possible delays.

evidence_trigger: Cause analysis: The planned migration to automatic key management rotated the Australia East storage key before either region could use its replacement.
evidence_fault: Cause analysis and impact: Both regions tried authenticating to storage with the invalidated key, causing identity management calls and some token requests to fail.

evidence_trigger: Response timeline: Disabling local authentication on the Cosmos DB account triggered customer impact.
evidence_fault: Cause analysis: The setting propagated to every replica, blocking ARM authentication to its feature-state dependency and preventing all ARM requests across US Government regions.

evidence_trigger: What went wrong and why: An underground feeder short tripped the datacenter breaker, cutting utility power.
evidence_fault: Impact and cause sections: One hall lost hosts; failed switches isolated replicas, disks became unavailable, dependent services lost access, gateways slowed, and apps returned errors.

evidence_trigger: What went wrong and why: The excerpt mentions a prior incident but does not identify what started the portal failures.
evidence_fault: What happened: Management portals failed to load content for some customers, while programmatic management and resource availability were unaffected.

evidence_trigger: Cause analysis: The GPT-5.2 update enabled settings that the production model engines did not support.
evidence_fault: Cause analysis: Incompatible settings reached the fleet, causing HTTP 400 errors. Incomplete capacity data later concentrated traffic in too few regions, prolonging HTTP 429 errors.

evidence_trigger: Description: Google traced the disruption to a configuration change and restored service by reversing it.
evidence_fault: Description and Customer Impact: Downstream services could not use IAM in Asia and returned errors when customers tried to create resources.

evidence_trigger: Description: The preliminary analysis identifies an invalid cross-project sink but does not say what event made it invalid.
evidence_fault: Description and Customer Impact: Subscriber messages accumulated, delaying log visibility until the sink was removed and the queue drained.

evidence_trigger: Description: Preliminary analysis identified a surge in incoming requests as the cause of the disruption.
evidence_fault: Description and Customer Impact: Increased load slowed responses and caused errors. Customers received HTTP 500 responses and could not reliably deploy applications.

evidence_trigger: Description: A configuration change introduced faulty feature-flag parsing; rolling back the change ended the incident.
evidence_fault: Customer Impact and Diagnosis: For service-account users, the gcloud process crashed with an AttributeError while parsing a feature flag.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: A configuration rollout set column-name normalization as the default for customers who relied on the previous behavior.
evidence_fault: Root Cause: Incomplete configuration left the API unable to handle the default. Detailed Description of Impact: The API rejected every affected customer’s load job.

evidence_trigger: Incident Report Summary: Cloud IAM began migrating to a different configuration management system on November 13.
evidence_fault: Root Cause and Detailed Description of Impact: Regions lacking the new verification keys rejected valid tokens, causing services to return incorrect 403 responses.

evidence_trigger: Description: Requests to create Service Networking connections peaked at ten times their normal level.
evidence_fault: Description and Customer Impact: Excess demand slowed Service Networking requests, causing instance creation to take longer, time out, or fail across dependent services.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: The capacity management service caused an invalid record to be written to the reservations database.
evidence_fault: Root Cause: The invalid record made available EU slots appear exhausted, preventing customers from purchasing slots or scaling up reservations.

evidence_trigger: Mini Incident Report, Description: GKE could not fetch affected drivers from a storage bucket owned by its GPU driver supplier.
evidence_fault: Customer Impact: Requests for affected driver installers returned HTTP 403, leaving some GPU nodes unavailable.

evidence_trigger: Mini Incident Report, Description: Google attributed the disruption to a configuration change detected by internal monitoring.
evidence_fault: Mini Incident Report, Description and Customer Impact: The faulty configuration caused Pub/Sub to reject requests across all API methods in three regions until rollback.

evidence_trigger: Mini Incident Report, Description: Google identifies crashes and overload but does not say what set them in motion.
evidence_fault: Mini Incident Report, Description: Crashes and overload-slowed cache refreshes left Chronicle’s API transfer service partially unavailable, delaying feed ingestion and downstream detections.

evidence_trigger: Description: Preliminary analysis linked the Search API failures to a new release of an internal service.
evidence_fault: Customer Impact: Some retail search queries failed more often or took longer than usual.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: A modest rise in customer traffic increased concurrent connections at one streaming backend cluster.
evidence_fault: Root Cause and Detailed Description of Impact: A backend connection limit caused requests to accumulate, overloading regional frontends; latency rose and most insertAll calls failed.

evidence_trigger: Root Cause: During scheduled hardware replacement, technicians disconnected the active switch instead of the redundant switch slated for removal.
evidence_fault: Root Cause, Remediation and GCP Impact: Partitioning left topology stale; congested links dropped packets and delayed traffic. Services returned errors; some disks became inaccessible.

evidence_trigger: September 28, opening paragraph: During a scheduled Codespaces secret rotation, operators skipped a checklist step.
evidence_fault: September 28, first two paragraphs: Components retained the old credential, disrupting port forwarding and Codespaces starts; jobs accumulated as VM pools drained.

evidence_trigger: October 13 incident, cause: GitHub traced the failures to a deployment that added a database validation.
evidence_fault: October 13 incident, impact and cause: Some records contained nulls where values were required, causing the Projects API to return errors on reads.

evidence_trigger: November 19 incident summary: A database host returned from scheduled maintenance with writes disabled.
evidence_fault: November 19 summary and mitigation: The host’s read-only state halted notification delivery. Delivery resumed once writes were enabled.

evidence_trigger: May 30 incident, cause: GitHub attributed the outage to a failure at the provider it relied on for authentication.
evidence_fault: May 30 incident, impact: Authentication failed, causing errors for every integration function except link previews.

evidence_trigger: August 5 incident, paragraph 1: GitHub began a planned database migration to remove a column from a pull request table.
evidence_fault: August 5 incident, paragraph 1: Some ORM queries still referenced the removed column, causing errors on up to 4% of web and REST API traffic.

evidence_trigger: December 22 recap: A sharp increase in requests, concentrated on search endpoints, started the incident.
evidence_fault: December 22 recap: Excess demand slowed unauthenticated page loads and API requests, sometimes to the point of timeout; authenticated traffic was unaffected.

evidence_trigger: May 6 incident: A routing configuration change unintentionally removed the route into the session service.
evidence_fault: May 6 incident: The faulty production configuration cut off inbound access, and every session API request failed until the rollback.

evidence_trigger: Cause: The runner version enforcement certificate expired because its replacement had been generated but not deployed.
evidence_fault: Impact and cause: Certificate expiry disrupted runner connections. Jobs queued, and reconnection traffic increased API load, response times, and server errors.
